title: Teluni Product Documentation
html:
This is the entry point for Teluni-specific product and architecture planning. The product owner's brief of 2026-10-17 is the source of the initial requirements. Engineering documentation is in English; product copy can be localized. Foundation-wide policy remains in the documentation task index.

Reading routes and ownership

Question Canonical document
What is Teluni, who uses it, and what is the commercial hypothesis? Product vision
What name/domains are approved, and which identity should be selected? Branding decisions and A/B/C studies
What belongs in the MVP, and how will it be accepted? MVP requirements and acceptance
What are the proposed components, modules, entities, and unresolved technical choices? Product architecture
How must publication, local playback, and recovery behave? Offline playback and synchronization
How can the residential pilot operate and later move to another host? Deployment and migration planning
What must tenancy, identity, data protection, and localization protect? Security and internationalization
What could prevent delivery or safe operation? Risks and dependencies
What is the phase sequence and current execution state? Implementation plan
Which decisions or external prerequisites need a human? Human actions

The owning contributor updates each document with changes to its subject, links related requirements rather than copying them, and regenerates the documentation portal through the contributing workflow. Stable requirement, decision, risk, task, and human-action IDs support traceability; they are documentation references, not implemented registries or API identifiers.

Meaning of status

Product/design status Meaning
Decided A product requirement or inherited accepted direction agreed for planning. It does not mean implemented.
Proposed A candidate solution or acceptance policy requiring evaluation/review. New ADRs remain proposed under the ADR process.
Pending An unanswered choice or investigation; no default has been silently selected.
Future Outside the MVP and not approved for immediate implementation.
Implemented Supported by repository code and verification evidence.

Task statuses (pending, in progress, completed, blocked, changed) have the separate meaning defined by the implementation plan. A completed documentation task establishes a specification, not a completed product capability.

Verified baseline

The manifest identifies a derived Teluni project, initialized from Orion commit 53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea. API composition is empty; web composition contains the core shell/portal only. There are no product tables/migrations, player application, media service, deployment manifests, or tenant workflows. The API runtime has health routes, configuration, telemetry, PostgreSQL infrastructure, and optional JWT access-token verification. These are foundation capabilities, not a working SaaS sign-in or tenant system.

This documentation stage does not authorize implementation, deployment, external publication, or acquisition of paid services. The plan identifies the next review and delivery gates.
